title: Is a condo linked to a train station a better buy?
excerpt: Every new project near an MRT or LRT station now calls itself a TOD. Sean explains what transit-oriented development means, who it suits, and the trade-off between convenience and security.

qa.context: With new MRT lines opening, developers market almost any project near a station as a transit-oriented development, or TOD. Mixed developments now combine homes, offices, serviced apartments, hotels and malls on one site, linked to rail.
qa.question: What is a transit-oriented development, and is a home in one a better buy?
qa.quote: convenience doesn't really come with security
qa.answer: A TOD is built around public transport, so residents can live, work and shop without relying on a car. That makes it strong for rental to young workers, but the same accessibility brings crowds, noise and weaker security, so it suits investors and singles better than families who want privacy.

reasons.title: Young tenants want the link
reasons.body: Workers in their first few years of employment can barely make ends meet, and a direct rail link saves them time and the cost of a car. That demand supports rents.

reasons.title: Easy access cuts both ways
reasons.body: When a station's commuters pass through a development, privacy suffers. High-end residents have even objected to stations near them, which is why expensive projects tend to be less accessible.

reasons.title: Someone pays for the walkways
reasons.body: Public link bridges and walkways need lighting, cleaning and guards. In some projects, residents' maintenance fees cover areas used by every commuter.

reasons.title: Compartmentalisation matters
reasons.body: In a mixed development, the residential part should be well separated from the mall, offices and station, or residents share their lifts and lobbies with the public.

actions: Ask whether the project actually connects to a station, or is merely near one.
Ask who maintains and secures the public walkways, and whether your fees pay for them.
Check how the residential block is separated from retail and transit areas.
Match the project to its tenants: TODs suit young workers who commute by rail.
Choose a more private development if security for a family comes first.
qa.caveat: Some projects are both rail-linked and highly secure, but they command a premium. Sean also questions whether buyers of RM1.6 million units, who seldom commute by train, need a rail link at all.

sourceNote: Summarised from Sean's English captions for this May 2018 video. The captions are of poor quality, so only points that are clear are included. The quoted line is verbatim; everything else is paraphrased.
